author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 산지의 혼합림에 사는 올빼미로, 낮에 활동하며 작은 새, 곤충, 쥐, 두더지 따위를 잡아먹는다. 딱따구리나 매가 쓰던 둥지를 이용하고, 알 자리에는 제 가슴 털을 조금 뽑아 깐다. 3~5월에 알을 3~10개 낳으며, 한국, 일본, 만주, 시베리아에 분포한다. 날개 길이는 23cm, 꼬리 길이는 18cm, 몸무게는 290g이다.

art.subject: Northern Hawk-Owl (Surnia ulula), adult (sexes alike, plumage the same all year), as seen in winter in Korea: forehead and crown blackish-brown, densely speckled with small white spots; whitish-grey facial disc framed on each side by a bold black crescent running from the crown sides down behind the cheeks; whitish eyebrows meeting above the bill; a black patch on each side of the hindneck, forming a dark V on the nape; upperparts dark brown spotted white, the scapulars with large white spots forming a pale band across the shoulders; wings dark brown with rows of white spots; underparts white, closely and evenly barred with narrow grey-brown bars from the breast to the vent; long graduated tail dark grey-brown crossed by narrow white bars; bill pale yellow; iris bright yellow; legs and toes densely feathered whitish.
art.pose: perched upright on a treetop in daylight, watching for prey
art.scene: Korean montane mixed forest in winter, snow on spruce, larch and birch branches, clear daylight; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, front view perched upright on a treetop: whitish-grey face framed by bold black crescents, dark crown densely dotted white, bright yellow eyes, pale yellow bill, white underparts finely and evenly barred grey-brown, feathered whitish feet, long tail hanging below

adult, side view perched upright: dark brown back and wings spotted white with a pale band of white spots across the shoulders, black V-marks on the nape, long graduated dark tail with narrow white bars projecting far beyond the wingtips
art.build: A medium-sized, slim, hawk-like owl, a little longer than a feral pigeon, with a long tail making up much of its length; much smaller than Ural Owl. Head rather small and flat-crowned, with no ear tufts. Bill short, strongly hooked, pale yellow, partly hidden in the face feathers. Legs and toes thickly feathered. Wings fairly short and pointed for an owl; at rest the wingtips fall well short of the tail tip, about the middle of the tail, so a long graduated tail projects beyond them. Sits very upright on the top of a conifer or bare tree, often raising or flicking the tail. Flies fast and low with quick wingbeats and glides like a sparrowhawk, swooping up to the next perch; sometimes hovers.
avoid: Do not add ear tufts or a large round head; the head is small and flat-crowned without tufts.
Do not paint the underparts buff or streaked lengthwise; they are white with fine, dense horizontal grey-brown bars, like a sparrowhawk's.
Do not paint a plain white crown; the crown is dark brown densely dotted white, and the pale face is outlined by bold black crescents.
Do not give it dark eyes or a short tail; those belong to Ural Owl (Strix uralensis). The hawk-owl has yellow eyes and a long tail.
